stem: A child has a significantly raised $Gal \: d1$ (Ovomucoid) level. What does this suggest about their clinical tolerance to egg?

options.text: They are less likely to tolerate extensively heated egg products like muffins.
They are likely to outgrow the allergy within the next six months.
They will only react to raw egg but can safely consume baked egg.
They are likely to have a cross-reactivity with chicken feathers.

explanation: Ovomucoid is heat-stable, so high levels indicate a likely reaction even to egg that has been baked.
rationale: Think about the stability of this protein when exposed to high heat.

optionExplanations.A: Ovomucoid is heat-stable, so high levels indicate a likely reaction even to egg that has been baked.
optionExplanations.B: While levels can be monitored over time, a high level at one point doesn't predict the speed of outgrowing the allergy.
optionExplanations.C: High ovomucoid levels suggest the opposite; the child is likely to react even to the baked forms.
optionExplanations.D: The source material focuses on clinical reactivity to food forms (baked vs. non-baked) rather than feather cross-reactivity.

source.hint: Think about the stability of this protein when exposed to high heat.
